items.prompt:
The most important points to emphasize are the:
A) salient points
B) smallest details
C) page numbers

Looking at your audience while presenting is:
A) eye contact
B) mumbling
C) reading the floor

Speaking loudly enough for all to hear is:
A) adequate volume
B) whispering
C) silence

Why support your claims with facts and examples?
A) it makes the presentation credible and convincing
B) it fills time
C) it confuses the audience
items.answer: A) it makes the presentation credible and convincing

steps: Evidence builds credibility. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) it makes the presentation credible and convincing

items.prompt:
A FOCUSED, coherent presentation:
A) stays on topic and flows logically
B) jumps between unrelated ideas
C) has no order
items.answer: A) stays on topic and flows logically

solution.answer: A) stays on topic and flows logically

items.prompt:
Which hurts clear delivery?
A) mumbling and speaking too fast
B) clear pronunciation
C) steady pacing
items.answer: A) mumbling and speaking too fast

solution.answer: A) mumbling and speaking too fast

items.prompt:
A student has 5 minutes to present research with lots of data. The BEST approach is to:
A) emphasize the most important findings and support them with key examples
B) read every statistic aloud quickly
C) skip the evidence
items.answer: A) emphasize the most important findings and support them with key examples

steps: Salient points + support. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) emphasize the most important findings and support them with key examples

items.prompt:
Which combination BEST describes an effective presentation?
A) focused content, relevant support, and clear delivery
B) random facts read in a monotone
C) a long story with no point
items.answer: A) focused content, relevant support, and clear delivery

steps: Content + support + delivery. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) focused content, relevant support, and clear delivery
